summary: Sizing formula adds 'modeled_costs' to a price distance without units, and the research doc drops costs from sizing entirely; SL losses exceed the risk budget by the cost share.
expected: Every term in risk_per_unit is quote-currency per unit of base, so realized loss at SL (fees + slippage included) is <= equity x risk_rate.
actual: The unit of modeled_costs is unstated; the ambiguity already produced the confirmed code bug (rate 0.0008 added to a 600 USDT distance).
impact: At $800 equity and 0.5% risk ($4.00), an SL at 0.5% distance loses about $4.64 (1.16x budget), at 0.3% about $5.07 (1.27x); with a taker entry up to 1.4x. The risk cap, the core safety rule, is silently exceeded on every tight-stop trade in backtest, paper and live.
evidence: RISK_MANAGEMENT.md:19-23 `risk_per_unit = worst_case_distance_to_SL + modeled_costs`; TRADING_STRATEGY_RESEARCH.md:551 `quantity = risk_budget / abs(entry - stop)` (costs only as later 'adjustments'); RESEARCH_PROTOCOL.md:91 `entry_fee` in 'basis points per side'; params fee_rate_entry = 0.0002 (a fraction). Probe (tmp/docs_trading_soundness/feasibility.py): cost share of R = (0.02%+0.05%+0.01%)/SL% = 0.27R at SL 0.3%, 0.16R at 0.5%, 0.08R at 1%; if entry is also taker 0.40R / 0.24R / 0.12R.
why_tests_miss: Golden fixtures are derived from the same formula; no test asserts 'loss at SL incl. costs <= allowed_risk'.
recommendation: Doc wrong -> use: risk_per_unit = |entry_worst - SL| + entry_ref x fee_entry_rate + SL x (fee_exit_rate + slip_exit_rate) (+ entry_ref x slip_entry_rate when the entry is a taker fill). entry_worst = adverse edge of the entry zone (LONG: entry_max; SHORT: entry_min). All rates are decimal fractions. Acceptance test: simulated SL exit P&L incl. fees and slippage >= -allowed_risk.
known_prior: KNOWN: ROADMAP Phase 11 (code bug in modeled_costs_per_unit); doc-level ambiguity not fixed by P11.

summary: No minimum stop distance or cost-to-risk ceiling; tight stops let fees and slippage consume the whole planned edge.
expected: A plan is rejected when round-trip modeled cost is a large fraction of the risk unit.
actual: Nothing in the docs prevents a 0.2-0.4% SL on a 1H setup, where costs are 0.2-0.4R, larger than the planning expectancy.
impact: Backtests on gross-favourable tight-stop setups become net-negative live; also inflates notional (0.3% SL -> $833 notional on $500), raising margin needs.
evidence: TRADING_STRATEGY_SPEC.md:69 has only `Maximum allowed stop distance: TBD`; no minimum. 00_PRODUCT_SCOPE.md:137-142 plans with expectancy +0.175R. Cost in R (maker in, taker out, 1bp): 0.27R at 0.3% SL, 0.16R at 0.5% SL.
why_tests_miss: No rule exists to test.
recommendation: Doc silent -> minimum safe rule: reject with NO_TRADE when (modeled round-trip cost per unit) / risk_per_unit > max_cost_to_risk (registry parameter; research baseline 0.15). Record the ratio on the plan. Needs a canonical rejection reason (decision required; do not invent a synonym).

summary: At $500 equity BTCUSDT rejects most swing stops (minNotional/utilization); the other live-5 symbols are feasible. The NO_TRADE rate is undocumented and the 60% rule creates a non-monotonic rejection band.
expected: The docs state which symbol/SL combinations are infeasible at the declared capital and require the NO_TRADE-by-reason rate to be reported.
actual: Rules are sound but their effect is unquantified; the 60% rule is non-binding except on BTC.
impact: Research results for BTC at $500 will not match what live can trade; minor (NO_TRADE is the safe outcome).
evidence: Probe tmp/docs_trading_soundness/feasibility.py (assumed prices BTC 60,000 / ETH 3,000 / BNB 600 / SOL 150 / XRP 0.60; filters from tests/fixtures/exchange_info_sample.json, recorded 2026-09-19: BTC step 0.001, minNotional 50; Binance 2023 announcement says BTC 100). $500, risk $2.50: BTC OK at SL <=2.08%, UTILIZATION_REJECT 2.08-2.5% (qty floors 0.00185 -> 0.001, util 0.55), OK 2.5-4.17% (qty 0.001, util 0.6-1.0), MIN_QTY above 4.17%. If minNotional is 100: NOTIONAL_REJECT for every SL > 2.08%. ETH/BNB/SOL/XRP OK at 0.5-5% SL. $1000: all OK up to 4-5%.
why_tests_miss: Design-level doc issue; tests encode the documented (or absent) rule.
recommendation: Doc correct (keep floor -> min checks -> 60% rule, NO_TRADE over round-up). Add: the backtest must run sizing at the actual live equity (e.g. $500 and $1,000), not a large notional, and report NO_TRADE counts by reason per symbol. A2 to confirm current BTCUSDT minNotional (50 vs 100).

summary: Slippage is defined on the entry of a LIMIT order (where there is none) and set to a flat 1 bp; stop-market exits, which suffer real slippage, get no explicit model; touch-vs-fill has no rule.
expected: Slippage applies adversely to every taker fill (STOP_MARKET SL, TAKE_PROFIT_MARKET TP, marketable entries). A resting limit fills at its price but only when price trades through it.
actual: A resting limit gets synthetic slippage, SL exits in fast markets get 1 bp, and a wick touch may count as a fill.
impact: Two optimistic biases: 1 bp on BTC/ETH SL is roughly the normal-market floor, and SOL/XRP stops in fast moves often slip several to tens of bps; touch=fill overstates fill rate on exactly the setups that reverse at the level (adverse selection). Expectancy is overstated by a few hundredths of R per trade, which is the same order as the planned edge.
evidence: RESEARCH_PROTOCOL.md:101-103 `effective_entry = intended_entry + slippage`; TRADING_STRATEGY_RESEARCH.md:698-710 'và tương ứng cho exit' (sign unspecified); params `expected_slippage = 0.0001  # 1 bps`, `slippage_model = "FIXED_BPS"`.
why_tests_miss: Fixtures encode the same FIXED_BPS assumption.
recommendation: Doc wrong -> use: (1) limit entry fills only if the 1m low < limit (LONG) / high > limit (SHORT) by >= 1 tick; touch-only is 'no fill' and is reported. (2) Every taker fill gets adverse slippage slip_bps(symbol), with a research baseline >= 2 bps on BTC/ETH and >= 5 bps on BNB/SOL/XRP, plus a mandatory 3x stress run. (3) Slippage sign is always adverse (LONG buys up and sells down; SHORT the reverse). (4) Calibrate from paper/live fills per protocol amendment.

component: Fee assumption vs entry order type
summary: Entry fee is modeled as maker (2 bps) although the entry is placed hours after the signal, may be marketable at placement, and no post-only (GTX) rule exists.
expected: Entry fee follows the actual liquidity role: a limit that is marketable when placed pays taker.
actual: Maker is always assumed. Exit taker is correct for STOP_MARKET/TAKE_PROFIT_MARKET.
impact: Underestimates cost by 3 bps on every marketable entry (about 0.06R at 0.5% SL); biases toward setups whose price is already inside the zone at approval time.
evidence: baseline-v3.toml:43 `fee_rate_entry = 0.0002  # 2 bps maker`, :44 `fee_rate_exit = 0.0005  # 5 bps taker`. EXECUTION_SPEC.md:27-31 entry `LIMIT or a defined limit-zone model`, no timeInForce. Binance USD-M regular tier: maker 0.02%, taker 0.05%, BNB -10% (finder.com, Binance fee page).
why_tests_miss: Design-level doc issue; tests encode the documented (or absent) rule.
recommendation: Doc silent -> minimum safe rule: backtest simulates placement at (signal close + modeled approval latency); if the limit is marketable at that moment the fill is taker (and at market + slippage). Live: either send entries as GTX (post-only; rejection = no trade, journaled) or size with the taker rate. Do not model the BNB discount.

summary: The canonical cost sets model every fill as 50% partial, a value chosen to work around hash normalization; it contradicts the FULL_FILL label and the 1.0 used by the baselines.
expected: Fill-model parameters are chosen from market reality and are identical between candidate and baselines.
actual: A serialization workaround sets a market assumption. At $60-$1,000 notional on BTC/ETH/BNB/SOL/XRP books, partial fills are rare; the real uncertainty is fill vs no-fill.
impact: A constant 50% fill halves realized risk (below the 60% utilization rule it is supposed to respect), halves $ P&L and drawdown, and makes candidate-vs-baseline comparison unlike-for-like. Paper/live parity (EXECUTION_SPEC 5) cannot hold.
evidence: baseline-v3.toml:53-57 `spread_fill_assumptions = "FULL_FILL"` ... `# Fractional value (NOT 1.0) to dodge the whole-number-trap (Pitfall 1)` `partial_fill_fraction = 0.5`; same in breakout-retest/baseline-v3.toml:55-61; baseline-no-trade-v1.toml:54 and baseline-simple-trend-v1.toml:56 use 1.0.
why_tests_miss: Design-level doc issue; tests encode the documented (or absent) rule.
recommendation: Doc wrong -> use: partial_fill_fraction = 1.0 for V1 order sizes (and the same value in all compared sets); model fill uncertainty with the trade-through rule (F-004). Fix hash normalization in the loader, never by picking parameter values. The loader should reject a partial fraction < minimum utilization.

summary: Nothing requires a live-price check after APPROVE. Price can cross the SL or leave the zone during the 4 h validity, so the LIMIT fills instantly and the SELL/BUY stop is rejected as 'would immediately trigger', leaving a naked position.
expected: Placement is refused when the current price has reached the SL (or the invalidation) since signal time or when the entry would be marketable beyond the planned zone; if an SL is rejected after a fill, the position is closed immediately.
actual: Docs define only risk re-check and plan-hash/expiry gates.
impact: Worst case: long approved after price already fell below SL -> buy limit fills as taker -> SL rejected -2021 -> unprotected position while the user is at work. Loss is unbounded by the plan (limited only by margin mode and liquidation).
evidence: EXECUTION_SPEC.md:16 `Risk re-check` (risk only), :55-65 item 4 'symbol/market conditions make the plan stale' (undefined); params signal_expiry_hours = 4. Binance error -2021 'Order would immediately trigger': a SELL stop needs stopPrice below the latest price, a BUY stop above it (Binance docs, New Order / New Algo Order).
why_tests_miss: Unit tests use static prices; no scenario moves price between approval and placement.
recommendation: Doc silent -> minimum safe rule: at placement read mark and last price; LONG: reject if min(price since signal) <= SL or current > entry_max + entry_buffer; SHORT symmetric; reject if the limit would be marketable unless the strategy spec permits marketable entries. After any fill, if the protective SL is rejected (e.g. -2021) or not acknowledged within N seconds, close with a reduce-only MARKET order, alert, and enter SAFE_MODE.
known_prior: KNOWN (partial): ROADMAP Phase 15 (price-vs-SL gate). The post-fill SL-rejection fallback is not in ROADMAP.

summary: Protective exits are placed only after the entry fill is observed; a LIMIT rests for up to 4 h, so if the process, host or user-data stream is down when it fills, the position is unprotected until restart.
expected: An exposure-creating order is never left on the exchange unless protection will exist even if the bot dies.
actual: No rule bounds the unprotected window or covers executor downtime.
impact: Single-host VPS restarts, DB outages (RUNBOOK 9) or network loss during a resting entry produce a naked leveraged position for hours.
evidence: EXECUTION_SPEC.md:18-22 `Place entry -> Place/attach protective exits`, :87-98 verification 'After entry fill'; RUNBOOK.md:33-42 handles a missing stop only once detected. PRODUCT_SCOPE.md:11-14: the user cannot monitor and cannot respond within minutes.
why_tests_miss: Design-level doc issue; tests encode the documented (or absent) rule.
recommendation: Doc silent -> minimum safe rule: (a) arm Binance's USD-M auto-cancel 'kill switch' (countdownCancelAll heartbeat) on symbols with resting entries, so normal (entry) orders cancel if the bot stops sending heartbeats (A2 to verify it cancels normal and not algo orders); (b) OR pre-place the protective SL as closePosition STOP_MARKET together with the entry if Binance accepts it with no open position (A2 verify); (c) SL must be acknowledged within a bounded time after the fill event (e.g. 5 s), else reduce-only market close + SAFE_MODE; (d) on graceful shutdown/SAFE_MODE cancel all resting entries.

summary: SAFE_MODE forbids 'new live order placement' without exempting protective or reduce-only orders, while the RUNBOOK asks to submit protection. Read literally, SAFE_MODE (entered exactly when a stop is missing) forbids placing the stop.
expected: SAFE_MODE blocks exposure-increasing orders only.
actual: The contradiction lets an implementer either never re-protect or treat SAFE_MODE as advisory.
impact: A position whose stop vanished (rejection, orphan sweep bug, manual cancel) stays unprotected until a part-time user reacts.
evidence: SECURITY_AND_OPERATIONS.md:80 `no new live order placement;`; RUNBOOK.md:33-42 `SAFE_MODE -> ... -> if stop is absent, submit protection only after risk validation -> otherwise require explicit manual intervention`.
why_tests_miss: Design-level doc issue; tests encode the documented (or absent) rule.
recommendation: Doc wrong -> use: SAFE_MODE blocks every order that can open or increase a position; reduce-only / closePosition protective orders and reduce-only closes are always allowed after an authoritative position query. Missing stop: auto re-place at the original plan SL (never wider); if price is already beyond the SL, reduce-only MARKET close. Manual intervention is optional, not required.

summary: workingType and priceProtect are never chosen. Binance defaults are CONTRACT_PRICE and false; priceProtect=true can stop an SL from triggering when mark and last diverge; the backtest price series must match the trigger series.
expected: The trigger price type and priceProtect are explicit, recorded on the plan, and matched by the backtest price series.
impact: Mismatch between the backtest (1m last-price klines) and live trigger; a priceProtect=true SL may not fire in a dislocation.
evidence: BINANCE.md:50 'Flags such as ... working type ... must be verified'; no doc selects values. Binance New Algo Order: workingType default CONTRACT_PRICE, priceProtect default false; when price reaches stopPrice the MARK/CONTRACT deviation cannot exceed the symbol triggerProtect (developers.binance.com New-Algo-Order). Liquidation is on Mark Price (Binance FAQ).
why_tests_miss: Design-level doc issue; tests encode the documented (or absent) rule.
recommendation: Doc silent -> minimum safe rule for V1: SL = STOP_MARKET workingType=CONTRACT_PRICE, priceProtect=false (guaranteed trigger, parity with last-price 1m backtest). Switching to MARK_PRICE requires backtesting on markPriceKlines. TP may use priceProtect=true. Record both on the plan and the constraint snapshot.

summary: Canonical docs treat leverage as read-only and never pick a margin type or require liquidation to lie beyond the SL. Risk-based sizing keeps effective leverage low, so the danger is concentrated in isolated mode at high account-default leverage.
expected: The margin type and leverage are set explicitly, and liquidation is verified to lie well beyond the SL.
actual: Orders inherit whatever the account has.
impact: Isolated + high leverage: premature liquidation (plus clearance fee) and a divergence from the backtest. Leverage 1x: entries rejected for margin when combined notional exceeds equity. Cross: one unprotected position can drain the whole wallet.
evidence: RISK_MANAGEMENT.md:89-91 'Leverage must be treated as an exchange/account constraint ... read current account/symbol constraints'; BINANCE.md:52-59 'read and record'. Arithmetic: $500, 0.5% risk: SL 0.5% -> notional $500 (1x per position, 2x for two); SL 0.3% -> $833 each. Isolated 50x -> liquidation ~2% - MMR from entry (inside a 2% SL); isolated 20x -> ~4.6%; cross -> effectively the whole wallet backs the position.
why_tests_miss: Design-level doc issue; tests encode the documented (or absent) rule.
recommendation: Doc silent -> minimum safe rule: margin type ISOLATED per symbol. Leverage set explicitly as the smallest integer L such that notional/L fits availableBalance with >= 20% headroom, capped at 5x. Guard: projected isolated liquidation price (bracket MMR from exchange) is beyond the SL by >= 1x the SL distance, else NO_TRADE. Refuse if the account mode differs and cannot be changed (open orders or positions).
known_prior: KNOWN: ROADMAP Phase 13 (leverage, margin type, liquidation guard) and Phase 14 (available margin).

summary: 'Account equity' is undefined (wallet vs margin balance vs available) and so is its timing (signal vs approval vs placement).
expected: One definition that cannot be inflated by unrealized profit.
actual: Undefined, and caller-injected in code (ROADMAP P12).
impact: Using totalMarginBalance with an open winner upsizes the next trade on paper profit; a stale equity oversizes after losses.
evidence: RISK_MANAGEMENT.md:7 'Risk is determined from account equity'; :20 `allowed_risk = equity x risk_rate`.
why_tests_miss: Design-level doc issue; tests encode the documented (or absent) rule.
recommendation: Doc silent -> minimum safe rule: sizing equity = min(totalWalletBalance, totalMarginBalance) of the quote asset (unrealized losses count, unrealized gains do not), snapshotted at plan creation and stored on the plan. At placement, re-read: if planned risk > risk_rate x current equity x 1.05, reject (re-plan). Never upsize. Backtest/paper: equity = simulated wallet balance with the same rule.

summary: The daily loss stop has no day boundary, PnL basis, equity base, comparison operator or reset rule; the docs say TBD while params fix 1%.
expected: An exact, reproducible definition.
impact: Inconsistent blocking between modes; the stop may reset mid-session with a restart or on a local-time boundary.
evidence: RISK_MANAGEMENT.md:51 `daily loss stop: TBD`; :71-85 NORMAL/WARNING/DAILY_STOP; params `daily_loss_stop_threshold = 0.01`, `daily_loss_warning_threshold = 0.005`.
why_tests_miss: Design-level doc issue; tests encode the documented (or absent) rule.
recommendation: Doc silent -> minimum safe rule: day = 00:00-24:00 UTC. daily_loss = -(realized PnL + commissions + funding) booked in that UTC day, from exchange data in live. Base = equity snapshot at 00:00 UTC. A state is reached when daily_loss >= threshold x base. DAILY_STOP persists across restarts until the next UTC day, cancels resting unfilled entries and never cancels protective orders. Note: 1% = two full losses at 0.5%; one slipped loss already reaches WARNING.

summary: Cluster membership and direction handling are undefined; with cluster_cap = risk_rate at most one aligned position is possible, so max_open_positions = 2 is reachable only as long+short in correlated coins. What counts as 'open' (working entries, pending approvals) is undefined, which allows two approvals to race past the caps.
expected: An explicit cluster and a consistent open-risk ledger.
impact: Either correlated double exposure (if the cluster is empty) or silent de-facto single-position operation.
evidence: RISK_MANAGEMENT.md:50 `max risk for one correlated cluster: TBD`, :57-59; params `cluster_cap = 0.005  # single-trade risk_rate`, `max_open_positions = 2`, `max_aggregate_open_risk = 0.01`.
why_tests_miss: Design-level doc issue; tests encode the documented (or absent) rule.
recommendation: Doc silent -> minimum safe rule: one cluster = all live-5 symbols (crypto beta), cap applied per direction. Open risk = filled positions (at original plan risk) + working entry orders + APPROVED-not-yet-placed plans. Gates are evaluated under one serialized lock at approval and again at placement. State explicitly that effective aligned exposure is one position.

summary: The approval message shows prices, R:R and 'risk %' but no quantity, notional, $ loss at SL net of costs, margin, leverage, liquidation price, or the equity used.
expected: A non-expert approving a live order sees exactly what money is at stake.
impact: The human cannot detect a sizing bug (e.g. F-001, or a wrong equity) before approving; the approval step provides no real check.
evidence: TELEGRAM.md:34-49 minimum contents; SIGNAL_AND_ALERTS.md:80-106 example `Risk: 0.5%`, `Valid until: 16:00 UTC`.
why_tests_miss: Design-level doc issue; tests encode the documented (or absent) rule.
recommendation: Doc silent -> minimum rule: add qty, notional, estimated $ loss at SL (gross and net of fees/slippage), $ at each TP, leverage and margin used, liquidation price, equity used with source and timestamp, current price and distance to entry/SL, and time remaining; values come from the risk pipeline output, never recomputed in the renderer.

summary: One 4 h validity is used for signal, approval and entry. There is no minimum remaining validity at approval, no exchange-side expiry, and no rule for how the user's availability (Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh office hours and sleep) biases which trades get taken.
expected: The approval deadline equals the plan expiry, and approval is refused when too little time remains for the entry to work.
impact: Late approvals place entries that are canceled minutes later (fees, orphan risk). Night-time (UTC 16:00-00:00) signals systematically expire, so user-executed results differ from system results.
evidence: `signal_expiry_hours = 4`; PRODUCT_SCOPE.md:14 'cannot guarantee response within minutes'; EXECUTION_SPEC.md:55-65. Binance GTD requires goodTillDate >= now + 600 s (New Algo Order docs; A2 to confirm for normal orders).
why_tests_miss: Design-level doc issue; tests encode the documented (or absent) rule.
recommendation: Doc silent -> minimum safe rule: approval deadline = plan.expiry_utc (measured from the source candle close). Reject approval if remaining validity < max(600 s, min_remaining_validity parameter). Entry is sent with GTD = expiry_utc as an exchange-side backstop in addition to the local cancel. The opportunity report slices by hour-of-day (UTC+7) to quantify the availability bias.

summary: 'Revalidated before approval/execution' does not say whether revalidation may change qty or prices, which would execute something other than what the human approved.
expected: The approved plan is executed exactly or not at all.
impact: Silent re-sizing after approval defeats plan-hash binding.
evidence: RISK_MANAGEMENT.md:143 'A plan calculated with stale constraints must be revalidated before approval/execution.'; TELEGRAM.md:23-30 approval bound to the exact plan hash.
why_tests_miss: Design-level doc issue; tests encode the documented (or absent) rule.
recommendation: Doc ambiguous -> use: revalidation is reject-only. Qty, prices and side of the approved plan are immutable; any change produces a new plan requiring a new approval.

component: TP ladder, breakeven, trailing, SL modification
summary: The TP1/TP2 template gives no quantity-rounding rule, and nothing says what happens to the SL after TP1 (breakeven? trailing?) or how to replace a stop without an unprotected gap.
expected: Leg quantities are floored to step with a deterministic remainder rule; stop management is either absent or specified and backtested identically.
impact: Rejected TP orders, an over-sized final leg, or a stop cancel/replace window without protection; backtest/live divergence if the live system moves stops the backtest does not.
evidence: EXECUTION_SPEC.md:77-83 `TP1 : TAKE_PROFIT_MARKET, reduceOnly=true, explicit quantity`; RISK_MANAGEMENT.md:61-65 only 'must not silently widen'. Example: BTC qty 0.003, TP1 50% = 0.0015 is not a multiple of step 0.001; qty 0.001 cannot be split at all.
why_tests_miss: Design-level doc issue; tests encode the documented (or absent) rule.
recommendation: Doc silent -> minimum safe rule: TP_i qty = floor(q x frac_i / step) x step; if any leg < minQty, use a single TP; the last TP closes the exact remainder (or closePosition). SL is closePosition (one-way) or qty == position. V1: no breakeven or trailing unless the frozen strategy spec declares it and the backtest simulates it. Any SL change may only tighten, and the new stop must be acknowledged before the old one is canceled (or the position is closed).

summary: Liquidation and auto-deleveraging (ADL), which close or reduce a position without our order, are not described beyond a LIQUIDATION_REPORTED status.
expected: Any position change not caused by our own order is detected and handled.
impact: Journal PnL and open-risk ledger drift; orphan protectives remain (covered by the sweep) but a partial ADL could leave SL qty > position.
evidence: GLOSSARY.md:109 `LIQUIDATION_REPORTED`; no mention of ADL or external close anywhere in docs (grep).
why_tests_miss: Design-level doc issue; tests encode the documented (or absent) rule.
recommendation: Doc silent -> minimum rule: reconciliation classifies unexplained position deltas (liquidation, ADL, manual) as EXTERNAL, journals them with exchange PnL, re-sizes or cancels protectives after an authoritative query, and enters SAFE_MODE if the position increased unexpectedly.

summary: 'Support the chosen position mode' vs 'support both'; the Multi-Assets mode effect on margin is unaddressed.
expected: A minimal supported scope with fail-closed detection.
impact: Hedge-mode templates (positionSide mandatory, no reduceOnly) are a large untested surface.
evidence: EXECUTION_SPEC.md:108-110; BINANCE.md:56-57.
why_tests_miss: Design-level doc issue; tests encode the documented (or absent) rule.
recommendation: Doc ambiguous -> use: V1 supports One-way + Single-Asset mode only; any other detected mode -> no new entries (fail closed) with an alert.

summary: The funding sign convention is 'documented' nowhere, 'ADDITIVE' is undefined, and funding intervals are assumed uniform.
expected: The Binance convention: positive rate means longs pay shorts; the fee = position notional at mark x rate, charged only if the position is open at the funding timestamp.
impact: A wrong sign flips a cost into income; multi-day swing holds (3-9 funding events) carry 0.03-0.1%+ of notional (about 0.03-0.2R at 0.5-1% SL), more in funding spikes.
evidence: RESEARCH_PROTOCOL.md:115 'Funding is signed per side per the documented convention'; params `funding_treatment = "ADDITIVE"`.
why_tests_miss: Design-level doc issue; tests encode the documented (or absent) rule.
recommendation: Doc silent -> use: funding_pnl = -sign(position) x qty x markPrice(fundingTime) x fundingRate for each actual fundingTime from the funding history (no fixed 8 h grid) while the position is open at that instant. Included in net R, not in sizing.

summary: Numeric pass thresholds are set only after Validation evidence from the three families has been seen, 'passing' is a human decision, and there is no multiple-testing correction across roughly 25+ variants plus parameter sweeps.
expected: Thresholds and the selection procedure are frozen before any out-of-sample data are looked at; the number of trials is recorded and penalized.
actual: Thresholds chosen after results = maximal researcher degrees of freedom; the user states little trading expertise.
impact: High probability of promoting a noise-fit variant to live (money loss), exactly the failure the kill gate is meant to prevent.
evidence: RESEARCH_PROTOCOL.md:211 'After >=3 independently specified families ... have produced Validation evidence, then and only then are candidate numerical thresholds proposed'; :236 'a family's passing status is a recorded human decision ... never computed'. Variant rows: trend-pullback 7, range-mr 11, breakout-retest 7+; plus sweeps (CONFIGURATION 8).
why_tests_miss: Governance, not code.
recommendation: Doc wrong -> use: before the first Validation run, a protocol amendment (v1.1.0) freezes the numeric gates: min trades overall/per symbol/per quarter; the lower bound of a block-bootstrap 95% CI of net expectancy > 0 at 1x costs and >= 0 at 2x costs; max drawdown and loss-streak ceilings at live equity. Every tried variant/parameter point is logged (trial count N) and a multiple-testing adjustment is applied (Deflated Sharpe, White's Reality Check, or Bonferroni). Exactly one pre-selected candidate touches the final holdout, once. A human decision may reject a numerically passing candidate but may never pass a failing one.

summary: 3-6 months of paper cannot statistically confirm the edge, and the exit gate ('minimum forward evidence defined by the actual signal frequency') is undefined.
expected: The paper gate tests what paper can test: operational parity and consistency with the backtest.
actual: Undefined gate; risk of reading 90 trades as proof.
impact: Either an endless soak or a false green light.
evidence: IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md:81, :98. BACKTEST_SPEC.md:101-107 own SE example. 15 trades/month x 6 months = 90 trades; sigma 1.2R -> SE 0.126R, 95% CI +/-0.25R versus a planning expectancy of +0.175R (PRODUCT_SCOPE:137-142).
why_tests_miss: Design-level doc issue; tests encode the documented (or absent) rule.
recommendation: Doc silent -> minimum rule: the paper exit requires (1) replaying the paper period through the backtest engine reproduces the same signals and plans byte-for-byte; (2) realized fill rate, slippage and latency are within the modeled assumptions; (3) paper net expectancy is not below the backtest block-bootstrap lower bound (consistency, not significance); (4) a pre-registered minimum n (e.g. >= 30 closed trades) and >= 3 months. Live starts at minimum capital.

summary: The research universe is chosen as '10-15 sufficiently liquid symbols' today, with no point-in-time rule, so survivorship and selection bias are built in (delisted or faded coins excluded).

summary: 'Periodically' and 'configured freshness threshold' have no values or classification; an unset threshold disables fail-closed.

why_tests_miss: Design-level doc issue; tests encode the documented (or absent) rule.
recommendation: Doc silent -> minimum rule (runtime config, non-null, fail-closed defaults): full REST reconciliation (positions, open orders, open algo orders) at start and reconnect and every <= 60 s while any position or working order exists (<= 5 min otherwise).
